skills.name: lamina
skills.description: Use passively for ordinary feature, product-behavior fix, user-flow refactor, and UI implementation requests in a Lamina-initialized repository, and explicitly for /lamina-init, /lamina-design, or /lamina-verify. Compile graph-backed product obligations into coding context and evidence gates. Skip purely mechanical build, formatting, dependency, and test maintenance.

skills.name: lamina-accessibility
skills.description: Specify and verify accessibility behavior on product-graph surfaces and workflows, including semantics, keyboard reachability, focus, errors, async status, and non-visual state communication.

skills.name: lamina-business-context
skills.description: Business context UX guidance. Use when bootstrapping Lamina for a project; answering business questions UX work needs; updating context after a pivot or scope change.

skills.name: lamina-competitive-analysis
skills.description: Reference patterns — learn from user-cited competitors or products as evidence. Not market parity slide decks.

skills.name: lamina-consistency-guarantees
skills.description: Product-facing consistency — what users and actors may see when, stale vs fresh data, and acceptable lag. Use when multiple views must agree without prescribing storage technology.

skills.name: lamina-content-design
skills.description: Copy and labels in contracts — scan-first labels, error text, and empty-state messaging. Use when screen copy blocks actor walks.

skills.name: lamina-controls-and-menus
skills.description: Actions and reversibility in contracts — primary/destructive actions, undo policy, confirmations. Use when destructive ops lack scenarios.

skills.name: lamina-core
skills.description: Lamina Problem Router — product design at the intersection of UX, product rules, and systems thinking.

skills.name: lamina-decision-making
skills.description: Prioritize contract gaps and verify findings — impact × effort, primary actor filter. Use when reconciling conflicts or ranking findings[].

skills.name: lamina-dependencies
skills.description: Map prerequisite, data, lifecycle, and reachability dependencies between typed product-graph nodes, including explicit behavior when a dependency is unmet.

skills.name: lamina-design
skills.description: Shape intended product behavior in Lamina's transactional graph when explicitly invoked as lamina-design or when passive implementation preparation reports design gaps. Publish an implementation-ready graph version without editing application source.

skills.name: lamina-design-process
skills.description: Agent-native design loop — domain contract, external build, verify, iterate. Not human workshop ceremony.

skills.name: lamina-discoverability
skills.description: Signifiers and affordances in screen contracts — actors must see what they can do. Use when actor walks report execution/evaluation gulfs.

skills.name: lamina-edge-cases
skills.description: Derive distinct product-risk scenarios from operations, dependencies, authority, lifecycles, concurrency, destructive actions, and recovery without generating exhaustive or duplicate edge-case lists.

skills.name: lamina-empty-states
skills.description: Empty and zero-data UX in scenarios — first productive action when domain collections are empty. Use when collection_empty scenarios are missing.

skills.name: lamina-error-handling
skills.description: Error and recovery UX in scenarios — slips vs mistakes, root cause in design not actors. Use when mapping failure scenarios in the active GraphVersion.

skills.name: lamina-evolutionary-rules
skills.description: Evolving product rules safely — reversible decisions, invariant checks as features change, deferring commitment. Use when the domain will grow or requirements are uncertain.

skills.name: lamina-feature-discovery
skills.description: Capability discovery — map requests to domain operations, workflows, and actors. Not generative research methods for human labs.

skills.name: lamina-feature-prioritization
skills.description: Scope prioritization — rank workflows by invariant risk and actor impact. Not roadmap theater or featuritis dogma.

skills.name: lamina-feedback-and-status
skills.description: System state visibility in contracts — modeless feedback, progress, and async status. Use when actors can't tell what happened after actions.

skills.name: lamina-feedback-loops
skills.description: Feedback loops in product behavior — balancing and reinforcing dynamics, delays, and oscillation. Use when state changes feed back into further change.

skills.name: lamina-field-research
skills.description: Live product grounding — repo and browser observation of real behavior. Not ethnography logistics.

skills.name: lamina-flow-design
skills.description: Design reachable actor workflows from typed product operations, dependencies, and terminal outcomes, including complete cross-actor handoffs and recovery.

skills.name: lamina-forms
skills.description: Form behavior in contracts — validation timing, field semantics, and recovery UX. Use when data entry blocks workflows or causes scenario gaps.

skills.name: lamina-heuristic-review
skills.description: Expert lens review — parallel contract, a11y, and invariant checks. Not Nielsen heuristic checklist theater.

skills.name: lamina-idempotency-concurrency
skills.description: Duplicate actions and simultaneous edits — double-submit, concurrent admin updates, and safe retries in product behavior. Use when shared resources can be mutated by multiple actors or requests.

skills.name: lamina-information-architecture
skills.description: Entity organization and retrieval — how actors find domain objects in screens and nav. Use when IA mirrors files or tables instead of tasks.

skills.name: lamina-init
skills.description: Use only when explicitly invoked as lamina-init. Establish business evidence and canonical Product, Actor, and Persona resources in Lamina's transactional graph.

skills.name: lamina-interview-design
skills.description: Actor-walk script design — probe operations, goals, and failure modes per simulated actor. Not human moderator craft.

skills.name: lamina-interview-documentation
skills.description: Walkthrough evidence — structured capture from browser/repo sessions. Not human session notes.

skills.name: lamina-invariants
skills.description: Product invariants — rules that must always hold, impossible states prevented, errors defined out of existence. Use when defining what can never happen in the product.

skills.name: lamina-leverage-points
skills.description: High-impact intervention points in product design — rules, information flows, and goals over UI tweaks. Use when local fixes fail to change behavior.

skills.name: lamina-modularity-boundaries
skills.description: Domain and feature boundaries — hide complexity behind clear ownership, pull complexity away from users. Use when splitting entities, actors, and responsibilities.

skills.name: lamina-multi-view-integrity
skills.description: Consistency across actor views — student, admin, and system surfaces must reflect the same domain truth. Use in multi-actor products when roles see different slices of one system.

skills.name: lamina-navigation
skills.description: Wayfinding in contracts — persistent nav, orientation, and hierarchy per screen. Use when actors get lost in verify walks.

skills.name: lamina-onboarding
skills.description: First-run and learnability — primary path without training, progressive power features. Use when new actors can't complete first workflow in verify.

skills.name: lamina-orchestrator
skills.description: Transactional product-graph workflows for design, source observation, Persona Missions, and runtime verification.

skills.name: lamina-persuasion-and-groups
skills.description: Multi-actor dynamics — group permissions, shared resources, and social side-effects. Not persuasion craft or influence tactics.

skills.name: lamina-platform-posture
skills.description: Product density — how much complexity the domain tolerates on each surface. Not sovereign/transient platform essays.

skills.name: lamina-problem-framing
skills.description: Design intake — align user request to domain scope, actors, and success outcome. Not pre-fieldwork research questions.

skills.name: lamina-product-behavior
skills.description: Represented model matches domain — UI must not imply illegal states or permissions. Use when the active GraphVersion domain and screens diverge from implementation shape.

skills.name: lamina-progressive-disclosure
skills.description: Progressive disclosure in contracts — essential vs advanced actions per actor. Use when novices overwhelmed or experts blocked on power features.

skills.name: lamina-quantitative-validation
skills.description: Metrics discipline — use only real user-provided data; suggest what to measure post-launch. No invented A/B results.

skills.name: lamina-requirements-definition
skills.description: Translate product intent into traceable critical promises, graph nodes, observable scenarios, assumptions, and scope without prescribing unnecessary implementation details.

skills.name: lamina-research-communication
skills.description: Findings communication — structured verify report for humans and coding agents. Not executive highlight reels.

skills.name: lamina-research-planning
skills.description: Simulation planning — plan actor walks, invariant probes, and walkthrough capture for verify. Not recruitment logistics.

skills.name: lamina-research-scoping
skills.description: Evidence scoping — what grounding is needed (repo, walkthrough, user input) vs assumption. Not human study scope.

skills.name: lamina-research-synthesis
skills.description: Simulation synthesis — merge parallel actor-walk and walkthrough results into findings[]. Not affinity mapping human interviews.

skills.name: lamina-side-effects
skills.description: Downstream effects of state changes — notifications, updates to related entities, and cross-actor handoffs. Use when one operation must trigger updates beyond the primary screen.

skills.name: lamina-stakeholder-alignment
skills.description: Multi-actor goal alignment — explicit trade-offs and permission conflicts in contract. Not org politics or workshop facilitation.

skills.name: lamina-system-structure
skills.description: Product system structure — entities, relationships, purpose, and quantities that change over time. Use when defining what exists in the product domain and how parts connect.

skills.name: lamina-system-traps
skills.description: Recurring product failure modes from system structure — policy resistance, shifting burden, tragedy of commons. Use when fixes keep failing or symptoms return.

skills.name: lamina-task-analysis
skills.description: Operations actors perform — map tasks to workflows and navigation. Use when workflows[] or IA don't match actor goals.

skills.name: lamina-time-semantics
skills.description: Define trustworthy date, time, deadline, expiry, recurrence, and timezone behavior. Use when a product accepts local times, crosses actor timezones, schedules recurring work, or triggers behavior from a clock.

skills.name: lamina-tradeoffs
skills.description: Surface consequential product-policy forks, reversible defaults, structural necessities, and desirability hypotheses so agents make coherent decisions without silently inventing product truth.

skills.name: lamina-trust
skills.description: Trust signals in contracts — transparency for payments, irreversible actions, and sensitive data. Use when actors hesitate on verify walks or scenarios lack honesty UX.

skills.name: lamina-usability-evaluation
skills.description: Actor evaluation — verify-phase simulated user walks on live product. Replaces recruit-N usability labs.

skills.name: lamina-user-modeling
skills.description: Create evidence-grounded Persona and Actor resources and compile independent graph Missions without treating simulations as research.

skills.name: lamina-verify
skills.description: Verify graph-backed product Missions after ordinary implementation work or when explicitly invoked as lamina-verify. Run isolated Persona and live UI audits; explicit verification is source-read-only.
